observation.visible_scene: A person wearing blue scrubs, a light-blue disposable bouffant cap, clear safety glasses, and a white pleated surgical mask is centered against a plain light-gray studio background. Throughout the first part of the clip one hand is raised to the face, fingers in contact with the mask around the nose bridge and mouth, as if fitting or pressing it. The head-and-shoulders framing stays constant, indicating a static camera.
visible_changes: From t=0.000 to about t=0.880 the raised hand remains at the mask, with only small positional shifts of the fingers and wrist while maintaining contact with the upper mask edge near the nose.
Between roughly t=0.960 and t=1.200 the hand releases the mask and travels downward, passing in front of the chin/neck and becoming motion-blurred.
By t=1.280 the hand has dropped out of the frame (only a faint blur at the bottom edge in t=1.200), leaving the mask in place over the nose and mouth.

From t=1.280 to t=3.200 the subject stands essentially still, facing the camera; the only visible changes are very slight head/eye micro-movements and the natural settling of the mask. The background and framing do not change.
The mask's coverage appears consistent once the hand leaves: top edge under the glasses, bottom edge over the chin.
outside_clip_unknowns: What preceded the clip (how the mask was initially placed and why the hand was already on it) is not shown.
What follows the clip (whether the person moves, speaks, or the hand returns) is not shown.
Whether the small finger movements constitute a deliberate adjustment or a hold/press cannot be confirmed from the frames alone.
uncertain_details: Exact handedness of the adjusting hand is ambiguous (it appears on the viewer's right, consistent with the subject's left hand, but could be the right hand crossing the body).
Whether the mask was pulled upward or merely pressed/positioned during the contact phase is not clearly resolvable.
Subtle apparent motion of the mask and body in the static tail may be breathing or minor sway rather than intentional movement.
The bright patches on the glasses are lens reflections, not separate objects.
